annotations.text:
Pick a direction, not a pixel.
Each board shows the same moment — the answer has just landed — in a different voice. Tell me which one to take further and I'll build out the full set of states (idle, asking, revealed, error) plus the phone layout.

A — PAPER ORACLE
Why: the ritual reads as something printed and permanent. Cream paper, ink circle, a real serif. Calm, unmistakably not another neon app, and effortlessly high-contrast for accessibility.
Tradeoff: quiet. Less "toy" than the object actually is — kids and casual users may find it stiff.

B — TOYBOX
Why: leans all the way into the toy. Thick outlines, hard shadows, a speech bubble that shouts the answer. Huge tap targets by default, and the most fun to shake.
Tradeoff: loud. The style dates faster, and Spanish strings run long inside a bubble sized for English.

C — AURORA
Why: closest to what you have now, but properly made — the orb becomes a light source, the answer surfaces from inside it, and the pause before it lands is the whole experience.
Tradeoff: the most familiar of the four. Dark-only means the glow has to carry it; needs a reduced-motion path from day one.

D — TICKER
Why: the different one. You type the question, so the answer sticks to something, and the tape keeps the day's readings. Turns a one-shot gag into something you come back to.
Tradeoff: new scope — an input, local storage, a clear-history control, plus a yes/no/maybe grouping of the 20 answers. Also the least magical: it reads like a tool.
